sections.text: In the beginning, when God created all beings by the sacrifice of Himself, He said unto them: Through sacrifice you can procreate, and it shall satisfy all your desires.
Worship the Powers of Nature thereby, and let them nourish you in return; thus supporting each other, you shall attain your highest welfare.
For, fed, on sacrifice, nature will give you all the enjoyment you can desire. But he who enjoys what she gives without returning is, indeed, a robber.

So we are now discussing Chapter 3, Karma Yoga, Yoga of Action. We typically evaluate before getting into any sphere of activity: What are my limitations? If I want to take a particular major in the university, am I good at mathematics, or am I good at science or arts? Once I decide what my limitations are, then I say how I can develop my capabilities in that field. And then that becomes the field of my choice.
So in Bhagavad Gita, Bhagavan in chapter two, give us our limitations. That Karmaniyeva adhikarahte ma faleshukajana. Our limitation is to act in the present only.
And we have no control over the fruits. So thats our limitation Bhagavan has given us. Therefore, Bhagavan said that do not worry about the fruits.
They are not in your capabilities. You never get attached to inactivity. You focus on your actions.
And then for development of my capabilities, then Bhagavan said, Yogastha Guru Karmani, establish yourself. Yoga is nothing but the balance of mind, equanimity of mind. So once you know your limitations that I have no control over the fruits, but I do have control over my actions, then I have to now become more efficient in my action. And therefore Bhagavan said that Yoga Isthaha.
Establish yourself in Yoga, you guys. Develop balance of your mind while acting. When your mind is imbalanced, there is no way you can act efficiently.
So once you establish the equanimity of your mind, then Yoga, Karma, Sukhaoshalam, that will be the result. You will become very efficient in your actions. You will be very dexterous in your actions if you can balance your mind.
So your job is only to balance your mind no matter what the situation is. Because you will be acting in this world in myriads of situations. Situations are not in your control.
They will be controlled by the world of phenomena, the world outside the people of the world. You have no control over that. But you have to continuously act.
Because you cannot stay without any activity. You cannot change the situation. But you can change the way you perceive and work in this activity.
In one of these TV serials, I heard a very interesting line: if you cannot change the Paristhiti, then change your Manasthiti. And I thought its a very profound statement. If you cannot change the circumstances outside, you can at least change your mental reaction to them.
Manasthiti, the state of your mind you can change because you cannot change the situation outside. The Bhagavan said Samatvam Yoga Ucha de balance of mind in all situations. Now that I have learned how to work efficiently, I need to know what is the field of my activity and what spirit I should be acting.
So the last verse we discussed is Yajnarthaat Karmano Anyatra Loko Yam Karmabandana Tad Artam Karma Kauntiya. Bhagavan has now given us the field of activity: Yajna is the field of your activity. And we have defined Yajna as cooperative activity for the greater good -- dedicated action, sacrifice.
So Yajna is basically people coming together in a spirit of sacrifice. Each one sacrifices something of his own for the betterment of the community. So Bhagavan said, thats the field and the spirit.
If you act with all the capabilities you have developed by that samatvam, employed in Yajna -- Lokoyam Karma Bandanaham -- actions performed other than for Yajna are binding. We know that action is bound by its own reaction. By the law of physics, Newton taught us in high school at least that action and reaction are equal and opposite.
Anytime there is an action, there will be a reaction. So the action is bound by the law of Karma. My actions are bound by law of actions.
So Im bound by the result of my action. Once I perform action, I have no control over the result. And as the actor I will be affected by the result.
So my action will have a reaction from the world. That reaction is now the effect of the cause which was my action. Now the reaction from the world when I react to becomes another cause for the reaction by the world.
So that chain starts the chain of cause and effect. Once I start the chain, I will be the only one who can break is I who can stop that chain by not reacting to the reaction of my action. So if I do not react to the fruit of my action, then Ill be able to break the chain of that action which I started.
Therefore, Bhagavan said Yajna Anyatra Lokoyam Karma Bandana -- actions which Im performing for gaining something, benefiting from my action, are all binding. All actions are binding. But if I am performing action not for me but for the greater good then Im not really expecting anything particularly for me and therefore there is no reaction from me and Ill stop that chain reaction.
Thats why Bhagavan said the karmas performed in Yajna are non binding to you as a person. Those karmas will be binding to the community for which you have performed that Yajna. Those karmas will be binding to the group of people benefit from those actions but not you personally.
So Bhagawan says therefore Yajnaartaat Karma, Kauntiya, Mukta Sangha, Samacharah without attachment, now you attach yourself into it. That Im doing this so that the community will benefit. That will also benefit me.
That attachment will again bind you. But if you are not attached to your actions in the first place and then to the results in the second place then you are completely free. So Mukta Sangha sam acharaha perform those actions.
And then the next verse now says that this is the universal design. This is not something Bhagavan said I came up with just to give you this advice. This is the original design, universal design, how this universe should function.
The next verse says Saha Yagnaha, Prajaha, Srushtva, Pura uvacha. Prajapati said that I created Yajna and Prajaya at the same time. So Praja here is all beings.
It is now narrowed down to human beings. Because everything in this world other than human beings working in compliance with the laws of nature, everything is cooperating and complementing each other except when it comes to human beings. We have free will and we become the disruptors if we are not working in this spirit of Yajna.
So Bhagawan said, when I created Praja, I also create a Yajna with it. There is a creative force in nature. That creative force is evolving things.
And when it comes to a level of evolution that you can function on your own, Prajapati says, I have created Praja but I also created the spirit of Yajna with it. By this you shall prosper. But Im giving you means to support yourself, means to prosper yourself.
This is your milch cow. This is your Kamadenu. And we obviously all know about the mythology of Kamadhenu the sacred cow which is capable of fulfilling all your desires.
So in mythology the cow came out of churning of ocean and it is also described as a cows body with human female head and birds wings. So it is basically combination of all beings. The this Kamadenu is all beings.
The birds and animals and human beings all working together can fulfill any desire. In this case your Yajna is the Kamadenu. This cooperative spirit and the actions performed in Yajna are capable of giving you whatever you desire.
When I created Praja, I created spirit of Yajna. We know that everything in this world has to be working together. And every one of us have to contribute our own share for the betterment of the community.
So if I am living in Hendrico county and enjoying all the services Hendrico county offers, I have to contribute my part as paying taxes. If every citizen decides that Im not going to pay my taxes, there wont be any services after a while. So Bhagavan said, you do your part, but if you work in this cooperative manner, you shall prosper.
You will get anything you desire by this Yajna. And the next verse says Devan Bhavayat vanena te Deva Bhavayantu vaha parasparam Bhavayantaha Sreiyah param avapshata -- Bhagawan explains how this cycle works. Cherish the Devas with this Yajna.
You nurture Devas with your cooperative actions. Because your existence in this universe is not that of an island. You as an individual, as you consider is not really an individual.
Youre just part of the big whole. And in this universe everything is connected to everything. And therefore if each part is not working in a right manner, which we call it Dharma Chakra, if thats not working, then there cannot be any progress.
There cannot be any evolution. Deva Bhavayatan -- we have discussed Deva before. Deva etymologically means that which is shining. So you know, in a vernacular language you have Diya, Deepak.
So Diva is that which is shining in human beings. Our senses are shining. Our senses illuminate the world outside.
So these senses can only work if I nurture those senses. So for me, even the individual to function properly, I have to nurture my senses. Then the same senses will nurture me.
Deva Bhavayantuvah, those Devas will then nurture you. You nurture Devas and Devas will nurture you in an individual level. If I take care of my senses, then my senses will nourish me.
At the universal level, the phenomenal forces are considered devas. So in our mythological stories, The Devas are 33 Karod Devas or 33 Koti. The 33 great elements are the devas.
Somewhere in his commentary, It has listed those Devas -- 8 Vasus, 12 Rudras, etc. In other words, everything in this world is important. Unless every element of this universe is taken care of, the universe cannot function as its supposed to.
Everything in the universe is working as per the laws of nature. The human beings have to be disciplined. And now, in todays situation, we all know about climate change, the green movement.
We know that world would have worked perfectly fine if we have not created the problem with the environment. Anytime I want to get something out of the environment, I have to make sure the environment is not affected. But which is where we are failing.
I actually read a very interesting theory on Facebook or WhatsApp -- the theory was that the coronavirus had come out because of the 5G network. The presenter was so convincing, and he related all the coincidences, saying when electricity was invented, then we had this great flu, and all the pandemics were related to the development in electricity and how we use it. And the latest is this 5G.
And the Wuhan was the main center of that 5G. Now there may not be any basis in this theory, but one thing is entirely possible, that if we do not use the natural resources with understanding, then it can create disasters which we have not anticipated. The global warming, we are all now experiencing the results of them.
So here Bhagawan said, you take care of the nature and nature will take care of you. How can I as an individual take care of the nature? Bhagavan said, if you act in the spirit of Yajna, that every action that you perform, if you analyze and see that it is for the greater good and not just for me. As Ezra Plate says, we will produce more than we consume, we will give more than we take.
If I have that attitude of Yajna, the sacrifice, Im sacrificing my actions for the greater good. Because you are cherishing Devas and those Devas, those phenomenal forces will then cherish you, will nurture you.

These verses reveal the cosmic design of mutual nourishment. When Prajapati created beings, he also created Yajna - the principle of cooperative sacrifice. The message is striking: this spirit of giving was not an afterthought but was embedded into creation itself. The Devas (cosmic forces or our own senses) and humans exist in a relationship of mutual support. We nourish the Devas through our offerings, and they nourish us in return. This is not mere ritual - it is the fundamental operating system of existence.
The verses warning is equally powerful: He who enjoys what nature gives without returning is indeed a robber. In our modern context, this speaks directly to how we engage with our environment, our community, and our own bodies. When we take from the earth without replenishing, when we benefit from society without contributing, when we use our senses without caring for them, we become thieves in the cosmic order.
Reflect today on the balance of giving and receiving in your life. Consider your Devas - your senses, your environment, your community. What have you received from them today? What have you offered in return? Identify one relationship where you have been more of a taker than a giver - perhaps with nature, with a colleague, or even with your own body. How can you restore balance through conscious offering? Remember: the Yajna is your Kamadhenu, the wish-fulfilling cow. When you give in the spirit of sacrifice, all your legitimate desires can be fulfilled.
